newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MICEX to start equity trading end of March.
newsitem.headline: Russian MICEX to start equity trading end of March.

text.p: The Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange plans to start equity trading at the end of March or start of April, the head of the exchange's equities department said on Tuesday.
"Our preliminary date, just for ourselves, is March 18, but it would be more realistic to name end of March or beginning of April as the starting date," Marina Medvedeva told Reuters.

MICEX will launch trading in Rostelekom telecoms company, utility Mosenergo and Norilsk Nickel metals group, Medvedeva said, adding that the exchange was in talks with national power grid Unified Energy System (UES) about its inclusion into the listing.
MICEX is Russia's biggest trading floor for hard currency and government securities. The trading system is based on a 100 percent deposit of paper and money to guarantee delivery.

Most share trading in Russia is done electronically through the Russian Trading System, a local version of NASDAQ. On another floor, the Russian Exchange has recently launched spot trading in Rostelekom, LUKoil and Mosenergo and futures trading for the same equities.
Medvedeva said MICEX would introduce an order-driven system for its equity trading, in which unnamed bids and offers with similar prices match within the system.

MICEX equity trading system would also have a market makers institution, whose functions would resemble those of primary dealers in Treasury bill trading. Primary dealers are the only one to have access to the system and all trading must be done through them.
Medvedeva said market makers would have to put out bid and offer prices for all shares every day and to support a certain spread between the prices.
She said one of Russia's biggest banks, Uneximbank would act as a depositor, while clearing and payments would be done by MICEX.
Medvedeva said 60 companies and banks had already became members of the MICEX share trading deaprtment and 30 more had filed applications.
